prompt: Order this cause-and-effect chain explaining how a mountain rain shadow forms.

options.text: Dry air descends the far slope and warms
Prevailing ocean winds hit coastal peaks
Leeward valleys stay arid behind mountains
Rising air cools and drops heavy rain

explanation: Ocean winds hit mountains, rise and drop moisture on the windward side, then descend dry and warm to create an arid leeward valley.

trap_notes.default: Moisture must condense and fall on the windward side before dry air descends to create a rain shadow.

prompt: Order how dark pavement and buildings create an urban heat island.

options.text: City air stays hotter than nearby farms
Dark asphalt absorbs sunlight all day
Rising heat increases air-conditioning use
Streets and roofs radiate stored heat at night

explanation: Dark urban surfaces absorb sunlight, radiate heat at night, warm city air above rural areas, and increase cooling demand.

trap_notes.default: Solar absorption by dark surfaces comes first, radiating heat that warms city air and drives up cooling demand.

prompt: Order the causal chain of seafloor spreading at a divergent ocean boundary.

options.text: New basalt crust pushes older seafloor aside
Tectonic plates pull apart under the ocean
Ocean basin gradually widens over millions of years
Hot magma rises into the spreading rift

explanation: Diverging plates open a rift, magma wells up to cool into new basalt crust, and older seafloor shifts outward as the ocean widens.

trap_notes.default: Plates pull apart first, letting magma rise to form new crust that pushes older crust outward.

prompt: Order the causal chain that produces a destructive coastal tsunami.

options.text: Shifted seabed lifts a huge column of water
Subduction earthquake snaps ocean floor upward
Waves slow and tower high near shallow coasts
Fast ocean swells race outward in deep water

explanation: An undersea subduction quake snaps the seabed up, launching fast deep-ocean waves that tower up upon hitting shallow coasts.

trap_notes.default: Seabed displacement launches fast low waves in deep water that only grow tall when slowed by shallow coasts.

prompt: Order how farm fertilizer runoff creates a coastal ocean dead zone.

options.text: Decaying algae consume dissolved oxygen
Rain washes nitrogen fertilizer into rivers
Low oxygen suffocates coastal fish and shrimp
Excess nutrients trigger massive coastal algae blooms

explanation: Fertilizer runoff feeds explosive algae blooms; when the algae die and decay, bacteria strip oxygen from the water, killing marine life.

trap_notes.default: Algae blooms themselves do not suffocate fish directly; bacterial decay of dead algae uses up the oxygen.

prompt: Order how hillside deforestation worsens downstream river flooding.

options.text: Loggers clear deep-rooted mountain forests
Muddy runoff clogs shallow river channels
Heavy rain washes loose topsoil down slopes
Overflowing rivers flood valley towns

explanation: Clearing forests removes roots that hold soil, so rain erodes topsoil into rivers, silting up channels and causing floods.

trap_notes.default: Root removal leads to soil erosion first, which fills riverbeds with silt and makes flooding worse.

prompt: Order how an El Nino event disrupts Peru's coastal fishing economy.

options.text: Warm water blocks cold nutrient upwelling
Anchovy schools shrink along the coast
Weakened trade winds let warm water drift east
Peruvian fishing boats bring in smaller catches

explanation: Weak trade winds allow warm Pacific water to pool off Peru, blocking cold upwelling, starving anchovies of plankton, and cutting catches.

trap_notes.default: Weakening winds shift warm water eastward first, which stops nutrient upwelling and hurts fish stocks.

prompt: Order the causal chain linking fossil fuels to coastal flooding.

options.text: Rising seas flood low-lying coastal cities
Extra greenhouse gases trap outgoing heat
Burning fossil fuels adds CO2 to the air
Warmer oceans expand and melt land ice

explanation: Fossil fuel combustion raises atmospheric CO2, trapping heat that warms oceans and melts glaciers, which raises sea levels.

trap_notes.default: Greenhouse gases trap heat first; warming then drives thermal ocean expansion and glacier melt.

prompt: Order how overpumping coastal wells leads to saltwater intrusion.

options.text: Freshwater pressure drops underground
Salty seawater seeps inland into rock pores
Coastal cities pump groundwater faster than rain refills
Municipal drinking wells turn brackish

explanation: Excessive pumping lowers underground freshwater pressure, letting dense seawater push inland and contaminate coastal wells.

trap_notes.default: Groundwater depletion lowers freshwater pressure first, which allows ocean water to creep into the aquifer.

prompt: Order how rapid rural-to-urban migration creates informal settlements.

options.text: Newcomers build makeshift homes on city fringes
Farm mechanization cuts rural jobs
City housing supply cannot keep pace with demand
Millions of rural workers move to megacities

explanation: Loss of farm work pushes rural migrants to cities; when formal housing falls short, newcomers build informal settlements on edge land.

trap_notes.default: Rural job loss drives migration first; housing shortages in the city then lead to informal settlements.

prompt: Order how standard shipping containers reshaped global factory locations.

options.text: Firms move factories to lower-wage Asian ports
Cranes load sealed metal boxes onto ships quickly
Ocean freight costs plunge for manufactured goods
Goods reach distant stores at competitive prices

explanation: Mechanized container loading cut shipping costs, letting firms offshore factories to lower-wage ports and ship goods globally.

trap_notes.default: Fast container handling lowered shipping costs first, making distant factory offshoring profitable.

prompt: Order how postwar US highways reshaped inner-city neighborhoods.

options.text: Middle-class families buy homes in outer suburbs
New interstate highways link cities to cheap farmland
Older downtown tax bases and transit shrink
Retail stores follow shoppers to suburban malls

explanation: Interstate highways opened cheap suburban land, drawing residents and retail out of central cities and shrinking urban tax bases.

trap_notes.default: Highways made suburban commuting possible first, pulling residents and shops outward and hurting downtown taxes.

prompt: Order the feedback loop triggered when Arctic permafrost thaws.

options.text: Microbes decay thawed peat and release methane
Warmer Arctic summers melt frozen subsoil
Extra methane traps more heat in the atmosphere
Faster warming thaws even deeper permafrost

explanation: Warming melts permafrost, letting microbes release methane that traps more heat and accelerates further Arctic thaw.

trap_notes.default: Initial warming thaws frozen soil first, releasing methane that amplifies further warming.

prompt: Order how summer heating drives the wet South Asian monsoon.

options.text: Moist Indian Ocean air rushes northward onto land
Intense summer sun heats India's interior plains
Heavy monsoon rains water South Asian rice fields
Warm rising air creates a deep low-pressure zone

explanation: Summer sunlight heats inland plains, creating low pressure that draws moist Indian Ocean winds ashore to drop heavy monsoon rains.

trap_notes.default: Land heating creates low pressure first, pulling moist ocean winds inland to produce rain.

prompt: Order how excess carbon dioxide in the air weakens coral reefs.

options.text: Seawater acidity rises and carbonate ions drop
Oceans absorb extra CO2 from the atmosphere
Reef fish lose shelter as coral structures crumble
Corals struggle to build hard calcium skeletons

explanation: Oceans absorb atmospheric CO2, raising acidity and reducing carbonate ions so corals build weaker skeletons and reefs degrade.

trap_notes.default: Ocean CO2 uptake lowers seawater pH first, depriving corals of carbonate needed to build skeletons.

prompt: Order the causal chain that built the Himalayan mountain range.

options.text: Granite crust buckles upward instead of sinking
Indian tectonic plate drifts northward into Asia
High snowcapped peaks block Asian air currents
Two continental plates collide head-on

explanation: The Indian plate drifted north into Eurasia; buoyant continental crust resisted subduction and buckled upward into the Himalayas.

trap_notes.default: Plate drift leads to continental collision, which forces crust upward into mountains that then alter climate.

prompt: Order how heavy irrigation in dry climates ruins fertile farmland.

options.text: Dissolved mineral salts stay behind in topsoil
Hot desert sun evaporates surface irrigation water
Farmers flood arid fields with river water
Salty crust stunts crop roots and cuts yields

explanation: Flooding dry fields brings trace salts; intense evaporation removes pure water while leaving salt in topsoil, poisoning crop roots.

trap_notes.default: Irrigation adds water containing trace salts; evaporation removes the water and concentrates the salt.

prompt: Order how melting ice sheets cause land in Scandinavia to rise.

options.text: Earth's crust slowly springs upward over millennia
Former sea beaches lift above modern coastlines
Mile-thick ice sheets press crust down into mantle
Post-ice-age warming melts heavy glaciers away

explanation: Heavy ice sheets depress the crust; when glaciers melt, the unloaded crust rebounds upward, lifting old beaches above sea level.

trap_notes.default: Ice weight must depress the crust and melt away before the land can spring back up.

prompt: Order how coal-fired power plants cause acid rain in distant forests.

options.text: Acidic rain leaches calcium from mountain soils
Prevailing winds carry sulfur dioxide downwind
Smokestacks release sulfur and nitrogen gases
Spruce trees weaken and lake fish populations drop

explanation: Smokestacks emit sulfur and nitrogen gases that travel downwind, fall as acid rain, strip soil nutrients, and harm forests and lakes.

trap_notes.default: Emissions enter the air first, drift downwind, fall as acid rain, and then damage soils and ecosystems.

prompt: Order how low birth rates create economic strain in countries like Japan.

options.text: Fewer young workers enter the labor force
Families have fewer children for several decades
Taxpayers struggle to fund pensions and elder care
Median age rises and retirees outnumber youth

explanation: Sustained low birth rates raise a nation's median age, shrink the incoming workforce, and leave fewer taxpayers to fund pensions.

trap_notes.default: Low birth rates shift the age structure upward first, reducing future workers and straining pension budgets.

prompt: Order how building a large upstream dam shrinks a coastal river delta.

options.text: Reservoir traps river silt behind the concrete wall
Ocean waves erode coastal farmland faster than buildup
Engineers build a major dam across a river valley
Clear river water reaches the sea with little sediment

explanation: Dams trap river sediment in reservoirs, starving the downstream delta of new mud so ocean waves erode the coast faster.

trap_notes.default: The dam traps silt upstream first, starving the delta of replenishment so coastal erosion outpaces deposition.

prompt: Order how Earth's tilted axis creates summer in the Northern Hemisphere.

options.text: Northern latitudes receive direct, concentrated sun
Earth orbits with its axis tilted 23.5 degrees
Longer days and stronger rays bring warm summer
North Pole leans toward the Sun in June

explanation: Earth's 23.5-degree tilt points the North Pole toward the Sun in June, giving northern latitudes direct sunlight and warm summer weather.

trap_notes.default: Earth's fixed axial tilt causes the North Pole to lean sunward in June, concentrating solar rays and warmth.

prompt: Order how Earth's rotation curves tropical trade winds westward.

options.text: Surface air flows back toward the hot Equator
Earth spins eastward faster at the Equator
Warm air rises at the Equator and cools aloft
Coriolis effect bends equator-bound winds west

explanation: Equatorial air rises and draws surface winds toward the Equator, where Earth's faster equatorial spin deflects them westward as trade winds.

trap_notes.default: Convection draws air toward the Equator, and Earth's rotation deflects that moving air into westward trade winds.

prompt: Order how a cold ocean current creates an arid coastal desert like the Atacama.

options.text: Chilled coastal air holds very little moisture
Cold Humboldt Current flows north along Chile
Coastal desert stays dry except for morning fog
Stable cool air resists rising to form rain clouds

explanation: Cold ocean currents chill coastal air so it holds little water and resists rising, leaving coastal deserts like the Atacama hyper-arid.

trap_notes.default: Cold ocean water chills the air above it first, preventing upward convection and leaving only coastal fog.

prompt: Order how daytime sunshine creates a refreshing afternoon sea breeze.

options.text: Cooler, denser air over the sea flows ashore
Afternoon sun warms beach sand faster than ocean
Warm air rises over land, lowering air pressure
Steady onshore breeze cools coastal towns

explanation: Land warms faster than water under afternoon sun, causing air over land to rise and draw cooler ocean air ashore as a sea breeze.

trap_notes.default: Land heats faster than water first, creating low pressure over land that pulls cool sea air inland.

prompt: Order the causal chain of skilled 'brain drain' from a developing country.

options.text: Trained doctors and engineers emigrate abroad
Local hospitals and schools face staff shortages
Wealthier nations offer higher pay and lab funding
Home country struggles to grow key public services

explanation: Higher wages abroad attract skilled graduates, leaving home hospitals and schools short-staffed and slowing local development.

trap_notes.default: Higher pay abroad pulls skilled workers out first, creating staff shortages that weaken home services.

prompt: Order how agglomeration economies build a specialized tech hub like Silicon Valley.

options.text: Skilled engineers and venture funds cluster nearby
Major research university spawns early tech startups
Region becomes a self-reinforcing innovation hub
New tech firms locate close to shared talent

explanation: Anchor universities spark early startups, attracting talent and capital that draw even more firms into a self-reinforcing hub.

trap_notes.default: Anchor institutions and early startups attract a talent pool first, which then draws competing and supporting firms.

prompt: Order how deindustrialization affected older Great Lakes manufacturing cities.

options.text: Younger workers move away to Sun Belt cities
Steel mills and auto plants close or automate
Cities face vacant blocks and shrinking tax revenue
Thousands of union factory jobs disappear

explanation: Plant closures and automation cut factory jobs, prompting workers to relocate and leaving older industrial cities with smaller tax bases.

trap_notes.default: Factory closures and job losses came first, triggering out-migration and then municipal budget strain.

prompt: Order how a shifting river course can spark an international border dispute.

options.text: Treaty defines a meandering river as the border
Diplomats negotiate a new border treaty or canal
Flooding cuts a new channel, shifting land to one side
Two nations claim ownership of the cut-off parcel

explanation: When a treaty uses a meandering river as a border, channel shifts strand land across the river, sparking disputes settled by diplomacy.

trap_notes.default: A river-based border treaty precedes the flood shift, which creates overlapping claims before diplomats settle it.

prompt: Order how Green Revolution crops increased groundwater depletion in Punjab.

options.text: Farmers pump deep aquifers with electric tubewells
High-yield wheat and rice need steady irrigation
Regional water tables drop year after year
Small farmers face rising costs to drill deeper wells

explanation: Thirsty hybrid crops spurred widespread tubewell pumping, which lowered water tables and forced farmers to drill costlier deep wells.

trap_notes.default: Water-hungry hybrid crops drove tubewell pumping first, dropping water tables and raising drilling costs.

prompt: Order how synthetic CFC gases thinned Earth's protective ozone layer.

options.text: More harmful ultraviolet rays reach Earth's surface
CFCs drift high into the cold stratosphere
Sunlight splits CFCs, releasing ozone-destroying chlorine
Spray cans and refrigerators leak CFC gases

explanation: Leaked CFCs rise to the stratosphere, where sunlight frees chlorine atoms that destroy ozone and let more UV radiation reach Earth.

trap_notes.default: CFCs must reach the stratosphere and break apart under UV light before chlorine destroys ozone.

prompt: Order how clearing coastal mangrove forests worsens cyclone storm damage.

options.text: Developers clear tangled mangrove roots for shrimp ponds
Coastal villages suffer deeper saltwater flooding
Cyclone waves sweep ashore without natural friction
Shoreline loses its natural wave-breaking buffer

explanation: Clearing mangroves removes tangled coastal roots that slow storm waves, allowing cyclone surges to sweep further inland and flood villages.

trap_notes.default: Mangrove removal destroys the natural wave buffer first, letting storm surges flood coastal towns.

prompt: Order how international migrant remittances reshape hometown economies.

options.text: Relatives spend funds on clinics, roofs, and tuition
Workers send part of their wages home via transfers
Migrants find higher-paying jobs in destination cities
Local builders and shops see steadier hometown sales

explanation: Migrants earn higher wages abroad and wire remittances home, helping families afford schooling and housing while boosting local businesses.

trap_notes.default: Earning wages abroad enables remittances, which families spend locally to stimulate hometown commerce.

prompt: Order how mass tourism can price residents out of historic city centers.

options.text: Longtime neighbors move out as rents climb sharply
Budget flights bring record waves of weekend visitors
Historic neighborhood shifts into a tourist district
Landlords convert apartments into short-term rentals

explanation: Surging visitor numbers push landlords toward short-term vacation rentals, turning residential blocks into tourist zones and raising rents.

trap_notes.default: Visitor surges motivate short-term rental conversions first, shrinking housing supply and driving up rents.

prompt: Order how overfishing led to the 1992 Atlantic cod moratorium.

options.text: Factory trawlers harvest cod faster than reproduction
Government bans cod fishing to save remaining stock
Spawning cod numbers crash to historic lows
Newfoundland fishing towns lose primary livelihoods

explanation: Industrial trawling outpaced cod reproduction, crashing spawning stocks and forcing a 1992 ban that devastated Atlantic fishing towns.

trap_notes.default: Overharvesting caused stock collapse first, which forced the government fishing ban and coastal job losses.

prompt: Order how tectonic rifting created East Africa's deep valley lakes.

options.text: Steep fault blocks drop down into a long rift valley
Rising mantle heat stretches African continental crust
Rain and rivers fill deep troughs into narrow lakes
Parallel cracks split the plateau north to south

explanation: Mantle heat stretches East Africa's crust, forming parallel faults whose sunken floor fills with water to create deep rift lakes.

trap_notes.default: Crustal stretching and faulting create the sunken rift basin first, which later fills with water as lakes.

prompt: Order how paving wetlands and prairies increases urban flash flooding.

options.text: Storm drains overflow into streets and basements
Concrete parking lots block rainwater from soaking in
Creeks rise rapidly in sharp, sudden flood peaks
Fast surface runoff rushes straight into storm sewers

explanation: Impervious pavement blocks soil infiltration, sending rainwater rushing into storm sewers so creeks peak sharply and overflow.

trap_notes.default: Blocking infiltration speeds up runoff into drains and creeks, which then surge and overflow into streets.

prompt: Order how a temperature inversion traps smog inside a mountain basin.

options.text: Exhaust gases build up in stagnant city air
Warm air layer settles above cooler valley air
Warm lid blocks polluted surface air from rising
Sunlight turns trapped exhaust into brown smog

explanation: A warm upper air layer acts as a lid over cool valley air, trapping car exhaust so sunlight cooks it into photochemical smog.

trap_notes.default: The warm-over-cool inversion layer acts as a lid first, trapping exhaust that sunlight turns into smog.

prompt: Order how blocking a maritime chokepoint like the Suez Canal affects global trade.

options.text: Container ships reroute thousands of miles around Africa
Stuck vessel halts traffic through the narrow canal
Stores face delayed goods and higher shipping prices
Extra fuel and weeks at sea raise freight costs

explanation: A blocked canal forces ships around Africa, adding fuel and transit time that raise freight rates and delay store deliveries.

trap_notes.default: Canal blockage forces longer voyages first, which raises fuel costs and then delays retail deliveries.

prompt: Order how frost wedging breaks high mountain cliffs into talus slopes.

options.text: Liquid water trickles into tiny cliff cracks
Broken boulders tumble down into steep rock piles
Expanding ice pries rock fractures wider apart
Nighttime freeze turns trapped water into ice

explanation: Water enters cliff cracks, freezes and expands at night, pries rock fragments loose, and drops them onto talus slopes below.

trap_notes.default: Water must enter cracks and freeze before ice expansion breaks rocks loose.

prompt: Order how a falling birth rate can create a temporary 'demographic dividend.'

options.text: Working-age adults outnumber young dependents
Rapid drop in birth rate shrinks the youth share
Higher savings and output boost national growth
Families and states spend less on child dependency

explanation: A sharp birth-rate drop leaves a large working-age generation with fewer dependents, freeing savings and labor to power rapid growth.

trap_notes.default: Falling fertility shrinks the child share first, creating a large workforce with lower dependency costs.

prompt: Order how Export-Processing Zones (EPZs) spark coastal urban growth.

options.text: Foreign firms build assembly plants in the zone
Government cuts tariffs and taxes near a seaport
Port city expands rapidly with new housing and roads
Thousands of workers migrate for factory wages

explanation: Tax-free port zones attract foreign assembly plants, drawing migrant factory workers and fueling rapid coastal city expansion.

trap_notes.default: Policy incentives at the port attract foreign factories first, which then draw workers and urban growth.

prompt: Order how a severe mountain wildfire degrades a city's drinking water.

options.text: Winter rains wash loose ash and mud off bare slopes
Intense wildfire burns forest cover and chars soil
Water treatment plants struggle with muddy reservoirs
Debris flows dump heavy silt into mountain streams

explanation: Severe fire strips vegetation and leaves water-repellent soil, so rains trigger muddy debris flows that foul downstream reservoirs.

trap_notes.default: Fire removes vegetation first; subsequent rains then wash ash and mud into streams and reservoirs.

prompt: Order how a stationary mantle hotspot built the Hawaiian island chain.

options.text: Pacific plate drifts northwest over the hot plume
Line of older extinct islands trails northwest
Magma plume punches through crust to build a volcano
Old volcano moves off plume and stops erupting

explanation: A stationary magma plume builds a volcanic island; as the Pacific plate drifts northwest, older volcanoes move off the plume and go extinct.

trap_notes.default: The hotspot stays fixed while the plate moves over it, carrying older volcanoes northwest to go extinct.

prompt: Order how social media spreads pop-culture trends globally.

options.text: Youth worldwide adopt shared slang, fashion, or music
Short-video platforms share clips across borders instantly
Local artists blend global styles with home traditions
Trendy dance or song goes viral in one major city

explanation: A trend emerges locally, spreads across borders via social platforms, gains global youth followers, and blends with local traditions.

trap_notes.default: A trend starts at a hearth, travels via digital networks, reaches global audiences, and then adapts locally.

items.text: Broad, gentle slopes of runny lava
Steep cone built of ash and lava
Explosive eruptions at subduction zones
Mauna Loa in Hawaii is a prime example

prompt: Classify each volcanic trait under Shield Volcano or Composite Volcano.
explanation: Shield volcanoes like Mauna Loa have broad slopes from fluid lava, while composite volcanoes form steep cones from explosive ash and lava.

trap_notes.default: Runny basalt lava builds wide shields; sticky magma creates steep, explosive composite cones.

items.text: Carries soil and sand away downstream
Drops sediment to build a river delta
Forms sandbars and coastal beaches
Carves canyons deeper into bedrock

prompt: Sort each landscape process into Erosion or Deposition.
explanation: Erosion picks up and transports weathered rock, whereas deposition drops that sediment to build landforms like deltas and beaches.

trap_notes.default: Erosion removes and moves material; deposition sets it down in a new place.

items.text: Sinking air brings clear, dry skies
Rising air cools into clouds and rain
Drives storms and tropical cyclones
Associated with calm, sunny weather

prompt: Classify each weather pattern under High-Pressure or Low-Pressure System.
explanation: High-pressure systems have sinking air that suppresses clouds, while low-pressure systems have rising air that forms clouds and storms.

trap_notes.default: High pressure = sinking air and clear skies; low pressure = rising air and stormy clouds.

items.text: Sun, Earth, and Moon line up straight
Sun and Moon pull at right angles
Produces mildest high and low tides
Occurs during full and new moons

prompt: Sort each tidal condition into Spring Tide or Neap Tide.
explanation: Spring tides happen at full and new moons when gravity aligns for extreme tides; neap tides happen at quarter moons for mild tides.

trap_notes.default: Spring tides are not about the season—aligned gravity makes tides 'spring' higher; right-angle neap tides are mild.

items.text: Reverses direction between seasons
Blows steadily toward the Equator
Guided sailing ships across tropics
Brings wet summers and dry winters

prompt: Match each wind system to Monsoon Wind or Trade Wind.
explanation: Monsoon winds reverse direction seasonally between land and sea, whereas trade winds blow steadily from subtropics toward the Equator.

trap_notes.default: Trade winds blow steadily year-round; monsoons flip direction between summer and winter.

items.text: Minority adopts majority dress and tongue
Diverse groups keep distinct heritages
Ethnic neighborhoods celebrate own roots
Original cultural traits fade over time

prompt: Classify each social pattern as Cultural Assimilation or Multiculturalism.
explanation: Assimilation blends newcomers into the dominant culture, while multiculturalism supports distinct cultural traditions coexisting.

trap_notes.default: Assimilation means blending into one dominant norm; multiculturalism means preserving diverse traditions side by side.

items.text: Full language used across different groups
Simplified trade speech, no native base
Uses small vocabulary and basic grammar
English in global aviation and science

prompt: Sort each linguistic trait into Lingua Franca or Pidgin Language.
explanation: A lingua franca is a full bridge language like English or Swahili, while a pidgin is a simplified contact speech with no native speakers.

trap_notes.default: A lingua franca is an established bridge language; a pidgin is a stripped-down makeshift trade speech.

items.text: Seeks converts across all nations
Tied closely to one people and homeland
Spreads mainly through birth, not missions
Christianity, Islam, and Buddhism

prompt: Classify each faith trait under Universalizing Religion or Ethnic Religion.
explanation: Universalizing religions welcome converts worldwide, whereas ethnic religions are closely linked to a specific culture or homeland.

trap_notes.default: Ask whether the faith actively seeks global converts (universalizing) or stays rooted in one heritage (ethnic).

items.text: Detached piece of a home country
Territory surrounded by a foreign state
Vatican City inside Rome, Italy
Alaska separated from the lower 48 states

prompt: Match each territorial example to Exclave or Enclave.
explanation: An exclave is a territory separated from its main state (like Alaska), while an enclave is completely surrounded by another state.

trap_notes.default: Ex- = outside/detached from the home state; En- = enclosed inside another country.

items.text: Extends 12 nautical miles from shore
Extends 200 nautical miles from shore
Grants resource rights, not full borders
Gives coastal nation full sovereign control

prompt: Sort each UN Law of the Sea rule into Territorial Sea or Exclusive Economic Zone.
explanation: A nation holds full sovereignty over its 12-mile territorial sea, and sole fishing/drilling rights in its 200-mile Exclusive Economic Zone.

trap_notes.default: 12 miles = full sovereignty (territorial sea); 200 miles = fishing and energy resource rights (EEZ).

items.text: Cargo shifts from ships to rail or trucks
Duty-free hub for re-exporting imports
Singapore or Hong Kong trade centers
Large loads split into smaller shipments

prompt: Classify each trade-hub trait under Break-of-Bulk Point or Entrepot.
explanation: A break-of-bulk point transfers cargo between transport modes, whereas an entrepot is a duty-free port for storing and re-exporting goods.

trap_notes.default: Break-of-bulk focuses on switching transport modes; entrepot focuses on duty-free re-exporting.

items.text: Clears tropical forest plots by burning
Herds camels, goats, or sheep in drylands
Follows seasonal grass and waterholes
Abandons depleted soil after a few years

prompt: Sort each traditional livelihood into Shifting Cultivation or Pastoral Nomadism.
explanation: Shifting cultivation rotates slash-and-burn crop plots in tropical forests, while pastoral nomadism herds livestock across arid grasslands.

trap_notes.default: Shifting cultivation grows crops in tropical forests; pastoral nomadism herds animals in drylands.

items.text: Rebuilds aging downtown blocks and parks
Spreads low-density suburbs over farmland
Increases car commutes and road costs
Redevelops blighted inner-city tracts

prompt: Classify each land-use trend as Urban Renewal or Urban Sprawl.
explanation: Urban renewal redevelops older central-city districts, whereas urban sprawl expands low-density, car-dependent suburbs outward.

trap_notes.default: Renewal rebuilds inside existing city cores; sprawl pushes low-density development outward.

items.text: Underground rock layer holding groundwater
Land area draining into one river system
Bounded on the surface by ridge divides
Tapped by deep agricultural water wells

prompt: Sort each water feature into Aquifer or Watershed.
explanation: An aquifer stores groundwater in porous underground rock, while a watershed is the surface land area draining into a river.

trap_notes.default: Aquifers are underground rock reservoirs; watersheds are surface drainage basins bounded by ridges.

items.text: Shades counties by color for income rates
Uses one dot per 1,000 residents
Shows exact clustering within regions
Applies uniform tint across whole state

prompt: Match each thematic map trait to Choropleth Map or Dot-Density Map.
explanation: Choropleth maps shade entire political units by statistical rates, while dot-density maps place dots to show spatial clustering.

trap_notes.default: Choropleth uses shaded areas for rates; dot-density uses individual dots for counts and clustering.
